title: Chapter 3. In praise of King Prataparudra
html:
Translated from Odia without a native speaker; doubtful places are marked (?) and (??). The original, transliteration and word-for-word translation are in the full edition (in preparation).

The third vritta (?) [section]1

3.1Sri Prataparudra is born in the Solar dynasty; he is a wondrous (?) avatara, a portion (?) of Vishnu.2
3.2. By serving Jaya-Durga [his parents] obtained him; since the mercy of the Supreme Lord was there, … (??).3
3.3. By his name the Gajapati dynasty is adorned in the realm (?); at his name the three worlds tremble.4
3.4. His company is the devotees of Vishnu, [like] wish-fulfilling trees; his mind abides in service to Vishnu's feet.
3.5. Noble, the best of men, the best among the jewels of kings — the Supreme Lord promptly (?) protects him.5
3.6. That King Purushottama is the refuge (?); he is his son, [the best] among kings (?).6
3.7. He is the sovereign of the earth of … (??)-khanda; the best of kings (?) made Southern Kataka his city.7
3.8. His boundless strength resides in the might of his arms; for the afflicted he becomes a support.
3.9. The treasures shankha-nidhi and padma-nidhi, it is told (?), are in his hand; and he himself serves Maharudra.8
3.10. By the power of Maharudra he is most mighty (?); by Rudra's grace all that is desired is fulfilled.9

Prataparudra's southern campaigns; Ghazi Ismail's raid on Puri; the Deity is hidden in Chadhei-guha

3.11That King Prataparudra was himself truly great (?): in the three worlds there remained not a single such (?) king.10
3.12. That king duly performed the golden bath; by [the rite of] the scales (?) he generously distributed (?) [gifts] to the people.11
3.13. How great (?) was his might in benta-bhiana! All the people (?) under the king knew no affliction.12
3.14. His army of seven akshauhinis was countless (?); from the arrows of his battle kings flee, routed (?).13
3.15. As he … (??) the land of Gauda, such a fate he dealt to Udayagiri [and] Chandragiri.14
3.16. That king thought of the great posts in the south, but of the Supreme Lord he did not think (?) at all.15
3.17. With thousands (?) of warriors, with a … (??) army (?) he went south; of the Supreme Lord he did not remember at all.16
3.18. At this time Ghazi Ismail, from … (??), marched to attack (?) and came to the kshetra (??) of Niladri.17
3.19. Mustering an army against Niladri, he marched; he said that he would take the Supreme Lord away.18
3.20. "We are the clan of servitors, the lowly servants of the Lord; we well know (?) this crooked design.19
3.21. … (??) in alarm (?) we all became … (??); we did not hand the Supreme Lord over to him.20
3.22. Having said so, we all took counsel together and resolved to open the secret southern door.
3.23. Towards the south, by the … (??) way, ran a secret passage; there we opened the bronze door.21
3.24. Seven little bells hung there on the door; when we opened [it], the vault (??) trembled at that sound.22
3.25. But (?) the Yavana could not make it out: we carried the Supreme Lord away, taking the seat of the brahma (?).23
3.26. By the secret southern door we went out; at …-natha (??) we placed the brahma."24
3.27. As soon as (?) the night grew deep, Narasimha seated Him (?) on an elephant and carried [Him] away.25
3.28. That Nrisimha Mahapatra is a wise man (?), the head of the clan of servitors, highly honoured,26
3.29. who is adorned with the office (??) of Pattajoshi; he carried the Supreme Lord away, rowing to the south.27
3.30. … (??) the Yavana (??) entered the fort of Kenkal (?); having bathed (?) in the lake, he obtained satisfaction.28
3.31. From that place, taking [Him], all the officers went; … (??) joined (?) [them], together with the Lord.29
3.32. In this way they carried the Supreme Lord away and placed [Him in] … (??), which was in the midst of the lake.30
3.33. That is the shore (?) of Chilika; there … (??). In that place the Lord stayed; … (??) the king … (??).31
3.34. A certain officer (?), seeing this, set out to the south and met the king on the bank of the river Krishnaveni.32
3.35. When that king heard such tidings, … (??).33
3.36. He said: "While I live (?), you report this to me as good news — that [someone] has given the Lord of our clan to the Yavana!"34
3.37. Then that officer, with folded hands, reported: "O king, we have safely hidden [Him] in Chadhei-guha."35
3.38. Hearing these words, the king became calm; he said: "This very day I will slay (?) [them] — what is a wretched Yavana [to me]!"36
3.39. Having spoken such firm words, the king, deeply moved, entered Chadhei-guha.37
3.40. In that place he beheld the Parabrahma and, exclaiming "Hari, Hari!", offered obeisance.38

Prataparudra's dream and initiation; the siege of Madara; Sri Chaitanya comes to Puri; the king learns of the young sannyasi

3.41The Supreme Krishna said: "Listen, O king: you … (??) the feet (?); these would have stayed (?) before (?).39
3.42. We would keep (?) … (??) [and] the throne in this place; taking all the bhoga, let them enjoy [it]."40
3.43. Such words he heard in a dream; from that day he accepted Vaishnava initiation (?).41
3.44. He became a mainstay (?) of the syllables of the name "Hare Krishna"; … (??) together with elephants he went to battle (?).42
3.45. … (??) having come to Madara, … (?) halted (?); the news arose that Prataparudra would come.43
3.46. All the troops did not make … (??); for a month they could not breach the fort of Madara.44
3.47. Having returned from there, the king showed his greatness (?); as a great Vaishnava he served the Lord in the city (?).45
3.48. For some days (?) he served the Lord … (??); [then] the king swiftly went to the southern quarter.46
3.49. The nine hundred (?) and eighteenth year (sal) began; thus, by good fortune, … (??) — when [He] entered.47
3.50. In Chaitra (?), the best spring month (?), at the time of … (??); at a youthful age … (??), at the time when He entered.48
3.51. With Him, in countless crowds, the Vaishnava fellowship; from the youthful face … (??) flow (?) [tears?].49
3.52. With a joyful face, with the name of Hari on His lips, He — the Moon of Shachi (?) — entered the Kshetra.50
3.53. Whose form is the full moon (?), [whose] bhava is guileless; staff and kamandalu are His natural adornment.51
3.54. Like a youth, [He shines with] a sweet smile (?); crying out the name "Radha, Radha," He sings most sweetly.52
3.55. [He], the moon of Nadia, came on the twelfth lunar day; the day … (?) was a Thursday, … (??).53
3.56. All went to see the young [sannyasi]; by the sight [of Him] life, eyes and mind are filled.
3.57. Step by step (?) [He] entered the Sri Mandir; at the cries of "Hari bol!" the universe shook.
3.58. That very Lord Gauranga granted darshan; whoever … (??) [this darshan] — for him the pious deeds of this birth bore fruit.54
3.59. Describing the hidden lilas with His lips, Gaurachandra went on, hearing [the chanting of] the names.55
3.60. All heard such words with their ears; [they] deemed themselves blessed, [their] birth greatly (?) [fruitful].56
3.61. From the Bhoga-mandapa building [they] received prasad; in the [temple] enclosure He, the embodiment of yoga (?), deeply [absorbed], … (??).57
3.62. For darshan all became agitated; the dandins (?) said: "This is a madman, a madman!"58
3.63. Thus some days passed; … (??) the Kshetra, … (??), [He] went to the south.59
3.64. Thus, when the month of Mithuna began, the king with his retinue (?) went to the service (?) of the Lord.60
3.65. [He] remains guarding the door of the anasara, … (??); in this service … (??) no one equals [him].61
3.66. This service, rare [even] for the gods, that king performs; for it he came, bringing … (?) [festive gifts].62
3.67. All the servitors took … (??); … (??) became pratiharis (door-keepers).63
3.68. All this he heard — of the doings (?) of the sannyasi whose mind always abides in Krishna's rasa.64
3.69. The whole story of Him Lenka narrated: "A young sannyasi-deva has come here."65

Tadhau reads the panjis; the praise of Gauranga; Ramananda Raya

3.70[The king] brought Tadhau, and [he], taking out the panjis, read: "A certain young vairagi has come (?).66
3.71. A circle of devotees came with Him; having seen the Supreme Lord, He went south (?).67
3.72. That Prabhu made the Kunja-matha His abode. Concerning this, O great one (?), be pleased to hear."68
3.73. Hearing [this], the king was truly (?) astonished: "We have heard of Him from … (?)."69
3.74. He is Sri Gauranga, the supreme devotee, the foremost … of Jagannatha …70
3.75. Gauranga, [my] life, is mother Shachi's darling child; Gauranga, [my] life, is the child of Jagannatha [Mishra].71
3.76. Gauranga, [my] life, is a sweet form; in the body of Gauranga, [my] life, is the light of the world.
3.77. In the feet of Gauranga, [my] life, is the poise of Natavara; on the body of Gauranga, [my] life, are the marks of the vajra (??).72
3.78. Gauranga, [my] life, is the avatara of a new ascetic (?); Gauranga, [my] life, is tender — [in Him is] the portion of Radha.73
3.79. On the neck of Gauranga, [my] life, are beads of tulasi; Gauranga, [my] life, is unhindered in various [fields of] knowledge (?).74
3.80. Gauranga, [my] life, is the treasury of all knowledge; Gauranga, [my] life, is the moon of Gauda …75
3.81. Gauranga, [my] life, is the husband of Lakshmi-devi; Gauranga, [my] life, is the understanding of all the scriptures.76
3.82. On the face of Gauranga, [my] life, is ever a line of smile; Gauranga, [my] life, proclaims (?) the explanation of the Vedanta.77
3.83. In Gauranga, [my] life, all knowledge is gathered; in Gauranga, [my] life, the primal root abides merged (?).78
3.84. Gauranga, [my] life, saw Gangadhara (?); Gauranga, [my] life, gazed with a sweet smile (?).79
3.85. The face of Gauranga, [my] life, is like the full moon (?); seeing Gauranga, [my] life, the three worlds are happy.80
3.86. Whoever … (??) beholds these [forms] even once, his sorrow of birth after birth is extinguished.81
3.87. Such is the glory of that Chaitanya Thakura: He is the lord of yogis of the whole earth.
3.88. The king had heard [of Him] from the mouth of Raya Ramananda, and resolved to meet the young ascetic at least once.82
3.89. By Providence that ascetic entered Sri Kshetra; there was a [great] gathering [of people] at the festival of Sri Gundicha.83
3.90. Here the name of Sri Gauranga became renowned; of this Sri Raya Ramananda heard (?).
3.91. He is the son of Bhavananda, the Karana (?); the best of villages, Bentapur, is his estate.84
3.92. He is the Pattajoshi (?) of Prataparudra; … (??) he is a devotee, unceasingly [full of] bhava.85
3.93. His mind is ever intoxicated with Krishna-rasa; ever in love for child Krishna, he is a devotee [whose devotion is] mixed with knowledge.86
3.94. He meditates on the Supreme Krishna; his consciousness is ever service in the mood of a servant.
3.95. His younger brother is Gopinatha; he is not … (??); with him … (??) the king (??); [his] mind is ever on Krishna.87
3.96. … (??) little by little [he] grasped everything; his royal duties went away, and Shachi's Lord became [his] all.88

Ramananda brings the king to Sri Chaitanya; the king questions the Guru about the tattva of Jagannatha

3.97[Ramananda] became a servant at the feet of Shachi's darling child; to introduce [Him] to the king he took great pains (?).89
3.98. Before King Pratapa … did (?), led (?) …90
3.99. Describing the glory of Sri Chaitanya Thakura, he brought (?) the king … (??).91
3.100. That king became enraptured (?) in devotion (?); his mind was always [turned] to Chaitanya Thakura.92
3.101. He is always firmly immersed in the name of Hari; [his mind] stays neither on the royal throne (?) nor in any other abode.93
3.102. When that bhava became manifest and arose, when Sri Gauranga Prabhu showed [him] mercy —
3.103. at that time that king was in our (?) company; joining his lotus (?) palms, he spoke before the Guru.94
3.104. He said: "O supreme Guru, hear (?) my words: you are indeed the crest-jewel of yogis.
3.105. To you indeed (?) [my] obeisance, most perfect … (??); you yourself are the complete … (??) of Brahman.95
3.106. You yourself are indeed an avatara, [a part] of Radha's body; you are indeed the essence of the treasury of all knowledge.96
3.107. You have indeed seen everything with your own eyes; you indeed know the glory of Jagannatha.
3.108. You indeed, then, in the Jagamohana — you indeed began (?) [it] at the time of the great dance;97
3.109. you indeed, rapt in the dance, carved (?) the stone and had the print of Sripada's lotus feet preserved there.98
3.110. At Sripada's lotus feet the Vaishnava's mind always rests; at Sripada's lotus feet is all (?) my entreaty.
3.111. You are indeed all-knowing, a seer of the three times; you indeed know [all] — [you are] a brahmarshi (??) and one who speaks of Brahman (??).99
3.112. Have mercy, O Prabhu, … (??) my doubt; may Mahaprabhu dispel [it] — let my doubt go.100
3.113. In my mind, O Prabhu, is this terrible doubt: Mahaprabhu uttered [a word] utterly abstruse (?).101
3.114. My countless sins will not (?) be destroyed — how then (?) will this offence be expiated (?)?"102
3.115. [He had] the wish to know in what tattva-form [the Lord abides]; therefore [the king] asked the Prabhu about the tattva of Jagannatha:103
3.116. "Dispel, O Prabhu, the doubt in my mind, O Antaryami! I am not a holy man … (??).104
3.117. He in Whose service Brahma and Shankara toil, Whose feet are served by … (??),105
3.118. Whose qualities Vani-devi is engaged in singing, Whose name Narada constantly remembers —
3.119. that Hari, the Maker of the universe, the divine Deity (?) — I am not capable of hearing His tattva (?).106
3.120. I am not a worthy vessel for this matter; but you have seen His face.
3.121. This we have seen with our own eyes: at the time of the dance the two lights touched each other.107
3.122. The blue and the white forms became one body; there the supreme light of the Pair shone forth.
3.123. You yourself are indeed a divine part (?); who would not accept those words … (??)?108
3.124. From your holy mouth all the devotees will hear … (??) words … (??) (?) …109

Ramananda at the Prabhu's feet; the secret of Jagannatha; Krishna in Dvaraka remembers Vrindavana

3.125You are indeed the cause (?) of the world's welfare; those matters we never know."110
3.126. Having spoken such sweet words, Ramananda Raya took refuge at the Prabhu's (?) feet.111
3.127. The Prabhu took hold of him, lifted him into His embrace, wiped (?) the streams of tears from [his] eyes and seated [him].
3.128. "That secret matter to which [you] at last (?) turned your mind — to that secret matter [I] have inclined (?) your (?) … (?)."112
3.129. "That secret (?) is the hidden … (??) knowledge of Brahman: He who is Jagannatha is Himself the son of the king of Vraja."113
3.130. [He] says: "There is no difference there, O devotees" …114
3.131. "That form is the essence of the pranava; His shape is not merely a body of bones (?).115
3.132. How (??) shall I reveal the mystery of this? So great is [this] bhava — only (?) with difficulty (?) is it attained (?)."116
3.133. Such was the essence of the matter the Prabhu expounded; I, the lowly one, wrote it down in a composition in the vernacular.117
3.134. Listen, O devotees, with a steady mind, to the account which [only] sages are worthy (?) to hear.118
3.135. In the Dvapara age Krishna left Mathura; leaving the flute, He came to Dvaraka, [to] the eight chief queens (?).119
3.136. There the Lord of Dvaraka brings deliverance (?) [to the world]; ruling as king, He destroys the wicked.
3.137. The swan of the heart-lotus (?) of men, He was enthroned in Dvaraka in royal attire.120
3.138. Raising (?) white umbrellas, the courtiers stand; learned (?) men daily recite panegyrics.
3.139. Telingi music plays at all times; the victory kettledrums stand ready (?) there.121
3.140. Holding the royal sceptre, that son of Vraja joyfully protects the people of Dvaraka.
3.141. Aguru and sandal pastes are applied [to Him]; the Prabhu … (??) in the kachhani of Vraja (?).122
3.142. A threefold (?) splendid necklace hangs on His chest; bracelets (?) and armlets (?) shine beautifully.123
3.143. Thus many days passed at that time (?); Sri Krishna's royal assembly, Sudharma, came into being (?).124
3.144. Gods, men and Yadavas are born (?) of His mercy; He Himself visibly became honoured (?) as king.125
3.145. His countless mercy has no limit (?); not even Mahamaya Herself knows its end.126
3.146. Radha and the other (?) yogeshvaris He did not even consider (?) in His mind; with Rukmini and the other wives the King of kings took delight (?).127
3.147. You have heard before, [O devotees,] that Radha is bhava incarnate (?); how then did He whose form is the Supreme Brahman leave Her?128
3.148. Can She who is full of prema ever abandon the Foe of Kamsa? [And] the beginningless Person [remembers] (?) Her love (?).129
3.149. Whenever He remembers that bhava of love, the illusion comes upon Him: "This is Vrindavana."130
3.150. Then (?) in Dvaraka He goes out and wanders through the city; holding the flute, He remembers the gopis in His mind.131
3.151. At once Lalita and the other eight friends gather; there King Narayana stages the rahasa.132
3.152. The night truly (?) becomes honey-sweet; taking the gopis with Him, the Prabhu immerses Himself in play.133

The rahasa in Dvaraka; the gopis ask Krishna to reveal His form as Rajendra

3.153There all the gopis engage in play; they adorn the face of the youthful Kishora with flowers.134
3.154. Such is the secret rahasa that Hari arranges; how much can I, a fool (?), set out in detail?135
3.155. Thus one (?) day all the cowherds — at the sound of the flute the cowherd boys (?) came and gathered.136
3.156. They were on the bank (?) of the Gomati, in the abode of rahasa; Lalita asked: "Listen, O life of the gopis!137
3.157. You indeed left the cowherds and went to Dvaraka; there, as Rajendra, You performed a royal lila.138
3.158. How beautiful is the splendour of Your kingdom! You enjoyed it, O Natavara — [and to us] You gave (?) humiliation.139
3.159. We are only cowherds; we have … (??) strength; You indeed know [our] hearts, O … (??) of Nanda.140
3.160. Show us mercy just once, O [Wearer of the] forest garland: we, all the cowherds, shall see Krishna as Rajendra.141
3.161. Of such good fortune, O Prabhu, You are the cause; Your name is the Wish-fulfilling Tree, Chintamani."142
3.162. Having said this, all the gopis prostrated themselves (?) [before Him]; at this time the … (??) of Nanda pondered in His mind.143
3.163. He said: "These indeed [have come] for Our sake; these … (??) abide in bhava — [Our] very life (?).144
3.164. … (??) … We indeed have the signs (?); they long for the form of Rajendra for Our sake (?)."145
3.165. Having pondered (?) thus, Krishna smiled slightly; becoming four-armed, He took up the conch and the discus.146
3.166. At once putting the flute to His lips in a graceful pose, the Prabhu stood forth (?) [before them] in the form of the King, Rajendra.147
3.167. On His feet shine (?) the tinkling anklets and little bells; on His feet gleam the bangles that steal the heart.148
3.168. … (??) the emerald plume looks beautiful; on His hips shines the pitambara.149
3.169. Over the pitambara is a jacket (?), most beautiful; on the jacket shine rows of gems and pearls.150
3.170. Over the jacket hangs a necklace of seven (?) strands; on the neck is a silver (?) chain set with pearls.151
3.171. On the head (?), on the garland (?) … (??) lovely; there is no forest garland there — [there is] a necklace of diamonds (?).152
3.172. The golden sacred thread gleams on the shoulder (?); rings (?) adorn the lotuses of the hands.153
3.173. On the lips is the flute, the pose is graceful, on the face a gentle smile; on the cheeks shines gorochana … (??).154
3.174. On all sides (??) shines the tilaka of musk; on the head (?) the crown (?), … (??) remains (?), sparkling (?).155
3.175. Row upon row … (??) the jewels (?) gleam there; [they] outshine the line of stars in a dark cloud.156
3.176. [He] put to shame (?) the full moon [and] the waves of the ocean; [He] outshines the beauty of dewdrops (?) on dark durva grass.157
3.177. In such beautiful attire the Dark One, the Bearer of the discus, stood before the gopis — the Slayer of Madhu (?).158
3.178. The gopis beheld Krishna-Chintamani in [this] attire; seeing [Him], Radhika rejoiced in her heart.
3.179. In the midst (?) of the royal assembly that Lalita was immersed [in bliss]; she herself began to dance before the Prabhu.159
3.180. Such was the wondrous form of Krishna-Chintamani; the gopis and the cowherds deemed (?) themselves fortunate.160
3.181. They beheld Krishna, the Lord of Dvaraka, in the assembly; before them they found Krishna, the King of kings.161

Krishna in Dvaraka cries out for Radha; the queens question Him and go to Vrinda

3.182The devotees contemplate the Root [of all], and the Guru of devotees contemplates [Him] too: only by bhava is Brahman, the great Meru, attained (?).162
3.183. In the rapture of bhava they saw the Krishna of the pastures; by their own (?) good fortune they earned (??) merit.163
3.184. Thus King (?) Krishna vanished from there and came again to the city of Dvaraka.164
3.185. Rukmini and Satyabhama served [Him], while He Himself set about managing (?) the affairs of the kingdom.165
3.186. [Yet] Hari always remains immersed in bhava (?): on the tablet of His heart He recalls the name of Radha, bhava embodied.
3.187. And so one day, in the abode of Dvaraka, [He] lay down on the couch with Rukmini in private (?).166
3.188. Satyabhama, the chief queen, [fans Him] with a peacock fan (?); all of them, those young wives (?), are absorbed in [loving] feeling.167
3.189. Then Krishna, in bhava, cried out and, holding the essence — Radha's name — on His lips, kept repeating [it].168
3.190. Hearing such a cry, the queens of Dvaraka said: "Prabhu, what (?) strange words are these?169
3.191. You are indeed omniscient, You know everything; You indeed create all that is in the universe.
3.192. You who by people's custom (?) did … (??) — how have You taken another woman's name into Your mouth?170
3.193. Moreover (?), the maidservants of Your feet are constantly beside [You]; at the hour of service, Prabhu, what conduct is this?171
3.194. In our presence, Lord, this is not fitting; dispel the doubt from [our] minds: how did this happen?172
3.195. Who is that woman called Radha? Who is that king of devotees whom You were remembering?173
3.196. If [You] do not tell all this, we shall fall into grief: [then], Lord, we shall not be worthy of Your lotus feet (?)."174
3.197. Hearing such words, the Prabhu, Chintamani, said: "Where did you hear this from My mouth?175
3.198. There is [one] named Vrindavati, … (??) a mistress (??); ask (?) her — she will tell you in detail.176
3.199. It is not seemly for Me to tell My own story with My own mouth; moreover, this story is exceedingly secret.
3.200. Whoever remembers (?) these stories, keeping them in the heart — into the cave of that one's heart I come and enter."177
3.201. When Sri Krishna had thus withdrawn, the two queens went and came to Vrinda.178
3.202. With joined palms they said with feeling (?): "Dispel the doubts in our hearts.179
3.203. Who is Radha? Of what land is that maiden? What are Her qualities, that She has bought (?) the Lord and taken [Him for Herself]?180
3.204. For Sri Hari is always distraught in the bhava of Radha; tell [us] who She is, and help (?) [us]."181
3.205. So Vrinda listened attentively (?); tears rained (?) down from her eyes.182
3.206. She said: "At your command! You have turned your minds to the story of Her who is the essence of Krishna's body, the light of the world.183
3.207. It is an exceedingly secret story — how shall I tell [it]? [For thus] I shall agitate (?) Krishna's mind.184
3.208. Wherever Radha's name is uttered, there Krishna will surely come at once and enter.185
3.209. How shall I tell [it]? If (?) I tell it, then the Lord of Dvaraka will come and enter here.186
3.210. If you wish (?) to hear this secret word, quickly call Yogamaya-Subhadra."187

Subhadra at the door; the story of Radha told in Dvaraka (here the text breaks off)

3.211Yogamaya-Subhadra will bar the door: she will not let Krishna, Rama and [the others] inside.188
3.212. Maya alone can hold back the Master of maya; then [I] shall be able to tell the story of Radha and Krishna."189
3.213. So (?) the queens did all this; Vrinda told the truth about Radha, expounding [it] in detail.190
3.214. Subhadra the door-keeper (?) sat … (??); they all listened to the secret truths.191
3.215. Rohini told the truths about Radha, reflecting (?) [on them], expounding in detail the … (??) glory of Krishna.192

Notes

  1. The chapter heading is printed ତୃତୀୟ ବୃନ୍ତ (tṛtīẏa bṛnta); on the word ବୃନ୍ତ cf. the note to 2.1 (in `../ch02/MP-02-1-28-en.md`). The heading stands on p. 14 after the colophon of Chapter 2 (after 2.210); Chapter 3 begins with it, and the numbering of the couplets starts again from 1.
  2. Prataparudra was the Gajapati of Orissa (reigned c. 1497–1540) and Mahaprabhu's patron in Puri (cf. the note to 1.32; Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 11–14). The same opening is found in the Vaishnava-lilamrita 4.1–4.2: the "Solar dynasty" (Surya-vamsha) is the self-designation of Kapilendra's dynasty, and "a portion of Vishnu" is courtly praise of the king. For Gaudiya Vaishnavas Prataparudra is a great devotee who swept the road before Jagannatha's chariot (CC, Madhya 13), but not an avatara in the theological sense. In the word ≈ ଅଂଶ (aṁśa, "portion") an extra sign resembling ନ is printed before ଶ (cf. 3.2, 3.3); possibly ଅଂଶେ ("as a portion"). The word ≈ ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ (adbhuta, "wondrous") is printed indistinctly.
  3. Jaya-Durga is the goddess Durga ("Victorious Durga"). The subject of "obtained" is not named — apparently Prataparudra's parents (cf. 3.6). There is no account of Prataparudra's birth by the goddess's grace in the Chaitanya-charitamrita or the Chaitanya-bhagavata. Printed ଜୟ ଦୁର୍ଗ ଙ୍କୁ with spaces and without ା; ଦୁର୍ଗାଙ୍କୁ is given. The last word is not identified: a T-shaped letter (ଦ or ହ), a sign resembling ନ, and ଲ; the rhyme with ଲଭିଥିଲେ requires the ending ‑ଲେ.
  4. Gajapati ("lord of elephants") is the title of the kings of Orissa. Before the last letter of the word a sign resembling ନ is printed (as in 3.1 and 3.2); understood as ମଣ୍ଡଳେ (maṇḍaḷe, "in the mandala, in the realm").
  5. The last word is printed indistinctly (≈ ସତ୍ତ୍ୱର); understood as ସତ୍ୱର (satwara, "promptly, without delay"), rhyming with ସାର (sāra).
  6. Purushottama is apparently the Gajapati Purushottama Deva (reigned c. 1467–1497), Prataparudra's father; "he is his son" is said of Prataparudra (the honorific ଅଟନ୍ତି, as in 3.10). Another understanding is possible: Purushottama is Jagannatha, who in Puri is honoured as the true king of Orissa, the Gajapatis being His servants; then "His sons are these kings". The words ≈ ଶରଣ (śaraṇa, "refuge") and ≈ ନୃପଗଣ (nṛpagaṇa, "kings") are read with doubt.
  7. The word ≈ କୁରମ (kurama) is not identified; it may be connected with Kurma (the tortoise, an avatara of Vishnu) and name a region, but the interpretation is unclear. Kataka (Cuttack) was the Gajapati capital; kaṭaka also means "royal camp". "Southern Kataka" may be Prataparudra's camp during his southern campaigns (cf. Vaishnava-lilamrita 4.6–4.7). ନଗ୍ର (nagra) = ନଗର (nagara, "city"). The last word is printed ≈ ନହୁବର; understood as ନୃପବର (nṛpabara, "best of kings").
  8. Shankha-nidhi and padma-nidhi are two of the nine treasures (nidhis) of Kubera, the god of wealth: the king is generous and rich. Maharudra is Shiva. The word ≈ ବଖାଣ (bakhāṇa, "as is told, renowned") is read with doubt: the second letter is a conjunct with a slanting stroke (ଖ or ନ୍ଧ; cf. 2.209).
  9. Prataparudra bears the name of Rudra. Gaudiya Vaishnavas honour Shiva (Rudra) as the greatest Vaishnava (Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.13.16), but regard worship of the demigods for the fulfilment of desires as a lower path (Bhagavad-gita 7.20–23); in the Chaitanya-charitamrita Prataparudra is a devotee of Jagannatha and Sri Chaitanya (Madhya 11–14). The last word of the first half-line is printed ≈ ଗଷିଷ୍ଟ: in this font the sign ରି resembles ଷ; ଗରିଷ୍ଠ (gariṣṭha, "most mighty") is given, ଷ୍ଟ being printed, apparently, for the rhyme with ଇଷ୍ଟ.
  10. From this couplet Kanai tells of Prataparudra's southern wars and of the Bengali army's raid on Puri, when the Deity of Jagannatha was carried away and hidden on Lake Chilika. The same story, largely in the same words, is in Madhava's Vaishnava-lilamrita, 4.4–4.23 (notes to VL 4.4–4.23). The Chaitanya-charitamrita and the Chaitanya-bhagavata do not describe this episode; cf. the note to VL 4.9 (Chaitanya-bhagavata, Antya 4: Hussain Shah, the sultan of Gauda, as the destroyer of the temples and murtis of Orissa). ବଡ଼ତ (baṛata), printed run together, is understood as ବଡ଼ ତ, "truly great". The word ≈ ତେହ୍ନ (tehna, "such") is read uncertainly.
  11. The "golden bath" (kanaka snāna) and apparently the tulā-puruṣa (weighing the king on scales against gold, which is then given to brahmanas) are royal "great gifts" (mahādāna). The first word of the second half is read uncertainly; ସମ୍ପିଲେ (sampile, "handed over, distributed"; possibly ସମର୍ପିଲେ) is printed with a dot above the line.
  12. Benta-bhiana is the clearing of forests and making of roads for an army; here, campaigns of conquest (cf. VL 4.4 and the note to it). The word ≈ କେଡୁ (keḍu) is understood as କେଡ଼େ ("how great"). ଜଣଇ (jaṇaï) is understood as "people" (ଜଣ, "person"); possibly ଜାଣଇ ("knows"). The sense of the second half is uncertain.
  13. An akshauhini is a complete battle division (in the Mahabharata, 21,870 chariots, as many elephants, etc.); "seven akshauhinis" is an epic hyperbole. ଅକ୍ଷଉଣୀ (akṣaüṇī) is a popular form. On p. 15 the sign େ is in places given as a small hook before the consonant (ବାଣେ, ନୃପେ here; also in 3.21, 3.22, 3.31, 3.32 and elsewhere). The words ≈ ଗଜଗଜ (gajagaja, "countless, teeming") and ≈ ଭଜା (bhajā, "flee"; possibly ଭଙ୍ଗା, "routed") are read uncertainly.
  14. Gauda is Bengal, the realm of Sultan Hussain Shah. Udayagiri and Chandragiri are fortresses in the south, the frontier of the Gajapatis' wars with Vijayanagara (cf. VL 4.7 and the note to it); ଉଦେଗିରି (udegiri) is a popular form. The first word (≈ ସାନ୍ତବେଣ୍ଟୀ) is not identified; its relation to ବେଣ୍ଟ (3.13) is unclear.
  15. Kanai reproaches the king: on his campaigns he forgot Jagannatha (cf. 3.17), and then the raid took place (3.18). ଠାଣ (ṭhāṇa) is a fortified camp or post. The last word ≈ ଚିନ୍ତିଲ (cintila, "thought of") is read uncertainly.
  16. Cf. VL 4.6: "with thousands of warriors, with a campaigning (?) army he again set out south" (ସହସ୍ରେ ବୀର ଦଣ୍ଡ (?) ସେନ). Here the print has ≈ ସସ୍ରେ (given as ସ[ହ]ସ୍ରେ), ≈ ଘଣ୍ଟ (not identified; VL has ଦଣ୍ଡ (?), "campaign, punishment", in this place) and ≈ ସେନ ("army").
  17. Ghazi Ismail was a general of Sultan Alauddin Hussain Shah of Bengal; around 1509–1510, while Prataparudra was at war in the south, he raided Orissa and Puri (cf. VL 4.9 and the note to it). ଗାଜ ଇସିମିଲ (gāja isimila) is "Ghazi Ismail". The word ≈ ଶୂର (śūra) is not identified (VL 4.9 has "from the north" in this place). The first word of the second half is printed as three signs (≈ ର/ଚ, ଡ, ଢ଼ି); understood as ଚଢ଼ି (caṛhi, "marching to attack"; cf. ଚଢ଼ଟି in VL 4.9). In the last word ≈ କ୍ଷେତ୍ରମେଳ the "kshetra" (Sri Kshetra, Puri) is clear; the end of the word is not identified.
  18. Niladri (Nilachala) is Puri. Kaṭaka means "army, camp".
  19. From 3.20 to 3.26 the speakers are apparently the temple servitors (sevakas) themselves, in the first person plural; to whom they are speaking is not said (possibly this is the officer's report to the king, cf. 3.34–3.37). ତ (ta, "indeed") may stand in place of ନ ("not"): "we do not know such crookedness".
  20. The first half is read only in part: the first word ≈ ଅଢ଼ (possibly ଅତି, "very"), ≈ ଆରତେ (ārate, "in distress, in alarm"), ≈ କାକରଥ (not identified; by the sense one would expect "alarmed", ≈ କାତର).
  21. ଗୋପତ (gopata, 3.22) means "secret". The word ≈ ରେଷବାଟେ is not identified (ବାଟେ — "by the way"). The bronze door is of bell-metal (kaṁsāra).
  22. The word ≈ ଗୁମ୍ଫଟି is read by the sense as ଗୁମ୍ଫ (gumpha, "cave, vault") + ‑ṭi; it is printed ≈ ଗ, ମ with a subscript sign, and ଟି.
  23. The "brahma" (brahma, 3.25–3.26) is, in Odia temple tradition, the hidden sacred substance (brahma-padārtha) within the Deity of Jagannatha, which is transferred into the new body when the Deity's body is renewed (nava-kalevara); apparently it is this that the servitors carried away, deceiving the Yavana. Gaudiya Vaishnavas, following Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, worship the Deity of Jagannatha as the Lord Himself, non-different from His form, not as a casing that holds some substance (cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 5: "You are not a pratima — You are the son of the king of Vraja Himself," said of Sakshi-gopala). ବ୍ରହ୍ମସ୍ଥଳ (brahmasthaḷa, "the seat of the brahma") is understood uncertainly. ମାତ୍ରକ (mātraka) is understood as "but".
  24. The word ≈ ବାଳିଲେକ is not identified; possibly ବାଳି (bāḷi, "sand") and ଲୋକ[ନାଥ] — Lokanatha, a temple of Shiva in Puri — but this is only a guess.
  25. Cf. VL 4.12: "Seating the Deities on elephants, Nrisimha Uparaya (?) leads [Them]." ମାତ୍ରରେ (mātrare) is printed with the same sign ତ୍ର as in ମାତ୍ର (3.16) and ପାତ୍ର (3.37); understood as "as soon as"; by the sense ମାଝରେ ("in the middle [of the night]") is also possible. The first letter of the word ≈ ତାକୁ (tāku, "Him") resembles ନ.
  26. Narasimha (3.27) and Nrisimha Mahapatra are the same person; in VL 4.12 he is called Nrisimha Uparaya (cf. the note to VL 4.12). Mahapatra is a title of rank. Printed ଅ, a space, ନ୍ତି; given as ଅ[ଟ]ନ୍ତି (aṭanti, "is", hon.; cf. 3.6, 3.10).
  27. Pattajoshi (paṭṭayośī; printed ≈ ପଠ, a broken sign, ଯୋଶୀ) is the office of the chief administrator of Jagannatha's temple (Pattajoshi Mahapatra). The word ≈ ପଦେଲ is understood as ପଦେ ("in the office"); the last letter is unclear. ବାହି (bāhi, "rowing"): the Deity was taken by boat (across Chilika, cf. 3.32–3.33).
  28. Gada-Kenkal (the fort of Kenkal) — cf. VL 4.11 and 4.19, where the servitors come with the Deities to the fort of Kenkal. The first two words are not identified (≈ ବୁଡ଼ି, ≈ ଯ + a small hook + ନ; given as ଯ[ବ]ନ, "Yavana"), so it is unclear who entered the fort and bathed — the Yavana or the servitors. The word ≈ ସ୍ନାହାନ is understood as ସ୍ନାନ (snāna, "bath"); possibly ସ୍ନାନ ଦାନ ("bath and giving of gifts").
  29. Printed ପ, a space, ତ୍ର; given as ପ[ପା]ତ୍ର (pātra, "officers"). The second half is read only in part: ମିଳି ଲ (possibly ମିଳିଲେ, "joined"), ≈ ଗଡ଼ଆମାନେ (not identified; possibly ଗଡ଼ୁଆମାନେ, "the people of the fort"), ଗହଳେ (gahaḷe, "together, in the company").
  30. ହରଦ (harada) = ହ୍ରଦ (hrada, "lake"); cf. VL 4.13: "in the midst of Lake Chilika, inside … (??) Chadhei". The word ≈ ଚୁମ୍ପିକ is not identified; possibly it is the same unclear word as ≈ କୁଁମାକ in VL 4.13 (understood there as "cave, shelter"). Printed ≈ ଉପୟରେ; given as ଉପାୟରେ (upāẏare, "in a way").
  31. Chilika is a large lagoon south-west of Puri (cf. the note to VL 4.13). The line is read only in part: ≈ ତଟ (taṭa, "shore"), ≈ ଅଟେ ("is"), after ସେ a gap in the print (possibly a word is missing), ≈ ଭିଆଣ ("arrangement"?); in the second half ≈ ନୃହ is not identified, and the end of the line (≈ ରା + fragments of signs) is broken.
  32. Cf. VL 4.14–4.15: "a Pana (?) set out to the south [and] on the bank of the Krishnaveni gives the king the news." Here the print has ≈ ପା + େ + ତ୍ର + କ; understood as ପାତ୍ରେକ (pātreka = ପାତ୍ର ଏକ, "a certain officer"); VL has ପାଣେକ (?), "a Pana". The Krishnaveni is the river Krishna in the south, where the king stood with his army.
  33. The second half is not understood: ≈ ଗୋଟାକ ସାତଟା ହେଲ ("one became seven"? — possibly an idiom for agitation or anger; cf. VL 4.16: "in anger he spoke"), then ≈ ଶୁ + a small sign, ବଂଶ ("dynasty"), ≈ ରା + fragments of signs (the end of the line is broken). Printed ବଖ, a space, ଣ; given as ବଖ[ଖା]ଣ (bakhāṇa, "tidings").
  34. Cf. VL 4.17: "While I live — what deed (?) is being done: the Lord has been given (?) to the Yavanas!" Printed ଥ, a space, ଉଁ; given as ଥ[ଥା]ଉଁ (thāu̐, "while I am"). The king apparently understood the news as meaning that the Lord had been handed over to the Yavanas.
  35. Chadhei-guha (the "Bird Cave") is a hill-island on Chilika where, according to Puri tradition, the Deities were hidden from raids (cf. VL 4.13, 4.18 and the notes to them).
  36. Cf. VL 4.21: "I will slay the Yavanas — what are they, wretched (?)!" Printed ମ, a dot, ରିଣ; given as ମ[ମା]ରିଣ (māriṇa, "having slain"); possibly ମରଣ (maraṇa, "doom [for them]").
  37. Printed ଗଢ଼; corrected to ଗାଢ଼ (gāṛha, "firm, strong") after the edition's list of errata ("୧୫।୨୯": page 15, line 29; by our count this is the 29th line of the page, so the number matches). In VL 4.19 the king contemplates the Deities in the fort of Kenkal.
  38. Parabrahma is a usual name of Jagannatha in Odia tradition. Gaudiya Vaishnavas, following the Brahma-samhita (5.1) and the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Adi 2), worship Krishna as the Supreme Personality of Godhead and regard the impersonal Brahman as His effulgence; for them Jagannatha is Krishna Himself.
  39. The account of p. 15 continues: in the Chadhei cave the king beheld the Parabrahman (3.40), and Jagannatha — "the Supreme Krishna" — speaks to him; by 3.43 this was in a dream. The Lord's speech (3.41–3.42) is understood only in part. "These" (emāna) are apparently the servitors who saved the Deity (3.20–3.37), whom the Lord bids to enjoy the bhoga (3.42); possibly "these" are the yavanas. The word ≈ ରହିଛ is not identified: printed ≈ ର, a sign like ନ୍ତ or ହି, and ଛ; tentatively understood as "you abide." ପଦ (pada) is "feet" or "rank, position" (the king's).
  40. The word ≈ ଛେଜ (cheja) is not identified; possibly a vernacular form of ସେଜ (seja, "couch"): "couch and throne." ଘେନଣ (ghenaṇa) = ଘେନିଣ ("taking"), as in 1.61. Bhoga is the food offered to Jagannatha; once offered it becomes prasad (cf. 3.61).
  41. The tradition that Prataparudra accepted Vaishnava initiation after a dream is not found in the Chaitanya-charitamrita or the Chaitanya-bhagavata. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita Prataparudra is a great devotee of Jagannatha who sweeps the road before the chariot (Madhya 13) and receives Sri Chaitanya's mercy (Madhya 14). The word ≈ ଦୀକ୍ଷା (dīkṣā, "initiation") is printed indistinctly (≈ ଦୀ + ଷା).
  42. Cf. Vaishnava-lilamrita 4.22: "Making the name of Jagannatha his japa beads, the king swiftly (?) sets out." ଧୁର (dhura) is "yoke, burden; foremost, chief"; understood as "mainstay, bearer" of the name; the first letter is ଧ or ବ. The word ≈ ଧେଇଣ is not identified (printed େ, ଧ, a dot, ଇଣ; possibly ଧାଇଁଣ, "rushing"). ସୁମର (sumara) is understood as ସମର (samara, "battle"); possibly ସୁମରି ("remembering"). ହୋଇଲକ (hoilaka) = ହୋଇଲେକ ("became").
  43. Madara (ମଦାର) is apparently Mandaragada, Garh Mandaran, a fort on the Orissa–Bengal border (cf. Vaishnava-lilamrita 4.23 and its note: "he drove off the mlecchas and reached the [place] called Mandaragada"). The subject of the first half-line is not named — apparently the yavana army besieging the fort (cf. 3.46). The words ≈ ଦୁରୁଣ (duruṇa; possibly ଦୂରୁଣ, "from afar") and ≈ ଗାଡ଼ (gāṛa, "trench"? or = ଗଡ଼, "fort") are uncertain. Printed ଉପୁଜଲ; given as ଉପୁଜିଲ (upujila, "arose").
  44. The word ≈ ଧାରି is not identified; possibly ଧାଡ଼ି (dhāṛi, "raid, onslaught"). After it the edition prints a "+" sign (apparently an editor's mark; there is no note to it below the line); it is not carried into the text. Sense: hearing that Prataparudra was approaching (3.45), the troops made no assault and in a month did not take the fort. ମାସକ (māsaka) — "for a month."
  45. Cf. Vaishnava-lilamrita 4.24: "He swiftly returned; but when he [again] set out to the south…". ବଡ଼ପଣ (baṛapaṇa) is "greatness, eminence"; "showed his greatness" is understood tentatively (a celebration of the victory?). ପଟଣ (paṭaṇa, "city") is apparently Puri or Cuttack.
  46. The last word of the first half-line is not identified: printed ≈ ପ/ଚ, a letter with a slanting stroke and ୁ, ର; possibly ଚତୁର (catura, "skilful, diligent"). Printed ≈ କଛିଦିନ; given as କିଛିଦିନ (kichidina, "some days").
  47. The year 918 is in one of the Odia "san" eras (Amli, Vilayati) or the Bengali san, which lag behind the Common Era by about 592–593 years, i.e. ≈ 1510–1511. By the accepted dating Sri Chaitanya came to Puri soon after taking sannyasa, early in 1510 (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 6). After ଶ in the word ≈ ନଅଶ (naaśa, "nine hundred," = ନଅ ଶହ) an unclear sign is printed (a broken letter?). The word ≈ ହେସର is not identified. ଯହୁଁ (yahu̐) is "when" (the same sign in 3.64). The subject of "entered" is not named — by 3.50–3.52 it is Sri Chaitanya.
  48. Madhu (madhu-māsa) is the spring month, in Sanskrit tradition Chaitra (March–April). The readings ≈ ଚୈତ୍ର (caitra) and ≈ ମଧୁମାସ (madhumāsa) are uncertain. The word ≈ ବେଣ୍ଟ (beṇṭa; cf. benta-bhiana, 3.13: "campaign") and the word printed ≈ ଯ + a sign like ଷ/ଶ (here, twice, and in 3.63 — ନବ + the same sign) are not identified; the latter is possibly ଯଥା (yathā, "when"), but ଥ on this page (ମିଥୁନ, 3.64) looks different. Printed କଶୋର (likewise in 3.51, 3.54); given as କିଶୋର (kiśora, "youthful").
  49. The second half-line is read only in part: ≈ ଜ୍ୟୋତ (jyota, "radiance"?), ≈ ପଡ଼ଅଶ୍ରୁ (possibly ପଡ଼ଇ ଅଶ୍ରୁ, "tears fall"), ≈ ଗଳ (gaḷa, "flows"?). The rhyme with ମଣ୍ଡଳୀ (maṇḍaḷī) is imperfect.
  50. Shachi is Sri Chaitanya's mother; "the Moon of Shachi" (śacīcandra) is He Himself (cf. "the moon of Nadia," 3.55, 2.170). The last letter of the word is printed with a subscript sign (≈ ଦ୍ର); possibly ଶଚୀନନ୍ଦ ("son of Shachi").
  51. The staff (danda) and the water pot (kamandalu) are the marks of a sannyasi. ଯାର (yāra, "whose"): the first letter is ଯ or ପ.
  52. "Sweet smile" is ≈ ମଧୁ ହସ (printed ≈ ଦସ); the verb ≈ ଚମକଇ (camakaï, "flashes") is uncertain. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita Mahaprabhu constantly sings the names of Krishna (e.g. on the way south, Madhya 7) and is absorbed in Radha's mood (Adi 4); in Kanai He cries out Radha's name — cf. the note to 2.203.
  53. Dvadashi is the twelfth lunar day. ଗୁରୁବର is corrected to ଗୁରୁବାର (gurubāra, "Thursday") by the edition's list of corrections ("୧୬।୧୫" — the line number matches our count). The word ≈ ମେଷ (meṣa) is uncertain: if it is the solar month Mesha (mid-April to mid-May), it does not agree with Chaitra in 3.50 (perhaps the day of Mesha-sankranti is meant). ଅଟଇହି (aṭaïhi, "was indeed") is uncertain; the last word ≈ ସର is not identified (ସାର, "best"?).

For Gaudiya Vaishnavas (following Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) the Deity's form is wholly spiritual — Krishna Himself, not a material shell (cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 5).
  116. The last word of the first half-line (≈ କେତେଣ) is not identified; by sense, "how" (possibly a corrupt କେମନେ). In the second half-line ≈ ଆଛେ ("is", Bengali), ≈ ସୁଦ୍ଧୁ (= ସୁଦ୍ଧା, "only, even"?), ≈ ମିଳୟେ ("is attained") and ≈ କଷ୍ଟେଣେ ("with difficulty", instrumental in ‑ଏଣେ) are read uncertainly.

  119. ≈ ଅଷ୍ଟପାଟ is taken as "the eight chief queens" (aṣṭa-pāṭa; cf. the aṣṭa-mahiṣī, Krishna's eight principal queens in Dvaraka, Bhagavata-purana, Canto 10); the reading and the syntax are uncertain. The editor's note mark (୧) is not carried into the translation.

Sārasa — a swan or crane (possibly "lotus"); the picture is of the Lord sporting like a swan in the lotus of the heart. ବିଜୟ is the honorific "to proceed, to be enthroned" (= ବିଜେ).   123. ≈ ଦୋସଡ଼ା ("double, two-stranded"?), ≈ କଙ୍କଣ ("bracelets") and ≈ କେୟୂର ("armlets") are read uncertainly.
  124. Sudharma — the assembly hall of the Yadavas in Dvaraka, brought by Krishna from heaven (Bhagavata-purana, Canto 10). ≈ ସେକାଳେ ("at that time") and ≈ ଜନିଲ ("came into being") are read uncertainly.
  125. ≈ ଜାତ ("born") and ≈ ବନ୍ଦିତ ("honoured"; possibly ବିଦିତ, "renowned") are read uncertainly; the link between the half-lines is unclear. There is no ॥ at the end of the line.
  126. Printed ପାଦ ("foot"); by sense given as ପାର ("limit, shore"). Mahamaya is the Lord's external energy.
  127. Printed ରୁକ୍ମଣୀ (without ି); given as ରୁକ୍ମିଣୀ — the same misprint in this word is corrected by the edition's corrigenda for p. 21 ("୨୧।୪"); there are no entries for p. 19. ≈ ଆଜ is given as ଆଦି ("and the others"; cf. the second half-line); ≈ ଭାଳିଲେ ("considered"; possibly ଭାବିଲେ) and ≈ ରମିଲେ ("took delight") are read uncertainly.   128. Printed ଭବରୂପୀ; given as ଭାବରୂପୀ ("bhava incarnate"; the ା has apparently broken off). Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 4: Radha is the embodiment of mahabhava. The question is addressed to the listeners (he, "O").
  129. The Foe of Kamsa (kaṁśāri) is Krishna. The second half-line is read uncertainly: ≈ ତାହାଙ୍କର ("Her") and ≈ ହେଜି ("remembering") are probable readings; the syntax is unclear.

  131. ≈ ଆଦି (lit. "beginning; and the others") is taken as "then, first"; the sense is unclear (possibly "the original Dvaraka").
  132. Rahasa (rāhāsa) is the Odia name of the rasa — Krishna's circle dance with the gopis; cf. Vaishnava-lilamrita 2.1 and the note there (where Kanai also builds the rahasa mandapa at Bata-Ganesha, 2.22–2.25). Lalita is the first of Radha's eight principal friends. "King Narayana" is Krishna as king of Dvaraka. The rasa with the gopis in Dvaraka is Kanai's own picture; according to the Bhagavata-purana and the Chaitanya-charitamrita, the rasa-lila takes place in Vrindavana, while in Dvaraka Krishna only remembers the gopis (cf. the note on 3.146).
  133. ≈ ଅବଶ୍ୟ ("truly, surely") is read uncertainly (printed ≈ ଅ + ବ + ଶ/ମ + ୍ୟ with ୁ).

  137. The Gomati is the river that meets the sea at Dvaraka. ≈ ତଟେଣ ("on the bank"; an archaic locative in ‑eṇa) is an uncertain reading. "The abode of rahasa" — cf. the rahasa mandapa that Kanai builds by Bata-Ganesha (Vaishnava-lilamrita 2.22–2.25; see the note to 3.151). Lalita speaks in 3.157–3.161 (the end of her speech is not marked in the text). She addresses Krishna with the respectful āpaṇa ("you"), but also with taba ("Your", 3.158, 3.161); the translation uses "You".
  138. Rajendra, "king of kings", is Krishna as king of Dvaraka (cf. 3.135–3.146). In ରାଜେନ୍ଦ୍ର, ରାଜ, ରାଜ୍ୟ, ପରାଭବ, ପରାଣ (3.157–3.166) the syllable ରା is printed with a sign resembling ଗ (the ା is indistinct); the reading follows the sense.
  139. Natavara — see the note to 3.77. ≈ ଦେଲ ("gave", 3rd person) is an uncertain reading; to whom "defeat, humiliation" (parābhaba) was given is not said: perhaps to the gopis, left behind for the sake of the kingdom, or to the enemies the king defeated.
  140. The last word of the first half-line (≈ କଚ୍ଛ) is not identified; by the sense, perhaps କିଛି / କିଚ୍ଛି: "we have no strength at all". For Gaudiya Vaishnavas (following Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) the gopis love only the Krishna of Vraja — Nanda's son in the dress of a cowherd boy; at the meeting in Kurukshetra Radha wishes not to see Him as a king but to bring Him back to Vrindavana (Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 13; cf. the notes to 3.146 and 3.151).   142. "Wish-fulfilling Tree" (bāñchā-kalpataru) — cf. the first couplet of the poem (1.1). Chintamani is the wish-fulfilling gem; here a name of Krishna (cf. 3.178, 3.180). କାରଣୀ ("cause") — cf. the note to 3.125.
  143. Printed ସ, a space, ଷ୍ଟାଙ୍ଗ(ି)ଲେ (without ା, the ି broken); given as ସାଷ୍ଟାଙ୍ଗିଲେ ("prostrated themselves fully", from sāṣṭāṅga). On the word after "Nanda" see the note to 3.159.
  144. The speaker is apparently Krishna (after 3.162: "pondered in His mind"); "We, Us" (āmbhe) is a respectful plural.   145. In the first half-line, after ≈ ଗବ (not identified) and the letter ଆ, there is a space and dots: text is missing in the edition. ≈ ଲକ୍ଷଣ ("signs") is an uncertain reading. The connection of the words in the second half-line is unclear.

Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17: when Krishna, hiding in a grove, assumed a four-armed form, the gopis, taking Him for Narayana, merely paid their respects and passed by, and before Radha He could not maintain that form; for Gaudiya Vaishnavas the gopis are attracted only by the son of Nanda.   148. ≈ ରାଜଇ ("shine") — perhaps ବାଜଇ ("tinkle"). Hāreṇī — "stealer [of the heart]" (feminine, for the rhyme with କିଙ୍କିଣୀ).
  149. The first two words (≈ ବଳା ଗୋଡ଼େ) are not identified; perhaps ଚୂଳା ("hair-knot", in which the plume is set) should be read for ବଳା. Markata piñchaka, "emerald plume", is the peacock feather — the mark of the Krishna of Vraja.
  150. Aṅgi, aṅgī — a jacket, coat (Odia); here part of the royal attire. The first ≈ ଅଙ୍ଗି is printed as ଅଙ୍ଗ with a superscript stroke.
  151. ≈ ସତ ସରି is taken as ସାତସରି, "a necklace of seven strands" (the ା apparently broken off); ≈ ରୂପସରି as "a silver (?) strand" (ରୂପା, "silver"); both readings are uncertain.
  152. The first half-line is only partly read: ≈ ମଦକ is taken as ମସ୍ତକ ("head"), ≈ ମଳରେ as ମାଳରେ ("on the garland"); ≈ ପୁଦ and ≈ ଶଣର are not identified (perhaps ପୁଷ୍ପ ଶେଖର, "a crest of flowers").   153. ସତ୍ର corrected to ସୂତ୍ର per the edition's list of errata ("୨୦।୨୦" — page 20, line 20; the line number matches our count).   154. Gorochana is a yellow pigment used for tilaka and for designs on the face. The last word (≈ ଉଧରସା) is not identified.
  155. ଶେଭଇ corrected to ଶୋଭଇ per the edition's list of errata ("୨୦।୨୨"; the line number matches our count). The first word (≈ ଚଉପଟେ, "on all sides"?) is badly damaged.   157. Printed ≈ ନିନ୍ଦଳ; given as ନିନ୍ଦିଲ ("put to shame"; the ି apparently broken off; ଳ given by norm as ଲ). The subject is not named — apparently Krishna's beauty. ≈ ଶୀକର ("spray, dewdrops") is an uncertain reading.
  158. "The Dark One, the Bearer of the discus" is Krishna. The last word (≈ ମଧୁହାରୀ) is taken as "the Slayer of [the demon] Madhu" (cf. Madhusudana); perhaps "the stealer of sweetness". The reading is uncertain.
  159. The royal assembly is the Sudharma (cf. 3.143). ≈ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ("in the midst") is printed with a damaged first letter. Āpaṇe means "herself" (Lalita) or "Himself" (the Prabhu); understood as: Lalita herself began to dance before the Lord. Cf. the dance in 3.108.
  160. ≈ ଗୁଣି is taken as "reckoning, deeming [themselves]" (or ଗଣି); the reading is uncertain.
  161. This is the last line of p. 20; the story continues on p. 21. In the second ରାଜ the ା is printed indistinctly.
  162. Continuation of p. 20: the gopis and cowherds see Krishna in royal form in the assembly of Dvaraka (3.165–3.181). Here apparently the narrator speaks.   163. "The Krishna of the pastures" (goṣṭha kṛṣṇa) is the Krishna of Vraja, the cowherd boy; the subject is apparently the gopis and cowherds (3.155–3.181). ≈ ଆପଣ ("own") is printed with a damaged second letter.   164. ରାଜନ (rājana) is taken as "the king" (cf. 3.181: "the King of kings"); a vocative "O king" is also possible — the narrator addressing his listener (perhaps King Prataparudra, cf. 3.100–3.103). ଅଂତର (= ଅନ୍ତର) — "vanished, withdrew" (cf. 3.201).

  166. ପହୁଡ଼ (pahuṛa) is the Odia word used in the Jagannatha temple for the Lord's retiring to rest (pahuda). Printed ପହୁଡ଼ଛନ୍ତି and ଦନ (without ି); given as ପହୁଡ଼ିଛନ୍ତି and ଦିନ. ≈ ରହସେ ("in private, in seclusion") is read uncertainly (≈ ର + ହ + େ + ସ); its rhyme with ଭୁବନେ is in the vowel only.   167. ହେଇଛନ୍ତି is corrected to ହୋଇଛନ୍ତି from the edition's errata ("୨୧।୭"). The first half-line is read uncertainly: ≈ ମୟୁର (= ମୟୂର, "peacock"; in this type ମ resembles ପ) and ≈ ସଞ୍ଚାଳ ("waving, fanning") are taken as a peacock fan with which the queen serves Krishna. The last word (≈ ବାଳୀ, "young women") may also be read as କାଳି ("at that time"); the letters ବ and ଗ are almost indistinguishable in this type. No ॥ at the line end.
  168. ଶତ୍କାର is corrected to ଚିତ୍କାର from the edition's errata ("୨୧।୮,୯" — the same misprint in lines 8 and 9, i.e. in 3.189 and 3.190). In the Gaudiya Vaishnava view, Krishna even in Dvaraka never forgets Radha and the gopis of Vraja (cf. the note on 3.146 and Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 13).
  169. Printed କସ (without ି); given as କିସ ("what kind of"). ≈ ବିପରୀତ ("contrary, strange, improper") — the third letter is printed with the sign for ରୀ (≈ ର with a vertical stroke). No ॥ at the line end. The queens address Krishna with the respectful āpaṇa ("You", hon.); rendered "You".
  170. The first half-line is read only in part. ≈ ଲୋକମତେ ("by people's opinion, by custom") is a probable reading (in this type ଲୋ is the hook େ + ଲ with an ା-tail; cf. ଲୋତକ in 3.205). The word ≈ ଅମାତ is not identified (its last letter is ତ with an inner loop; possibly ଅମାତ୍ୟ or ଅମାନ୍ୟ). No ॥ at the line end.
  171. ଖଣୀ is corrected to ଖଟଣୀ from the edition's errata ("୨୧।୧୨"; in the print a damaged colon-like sign stands in place of ଟ). Khaṭaṇi is Odia for "service, turn of duty" (also used of the shifts of temple servants). "The maidservants of [Your] feet" (caraṇa dāsī) are the queens themselves. The first word (≈ ଆବର) is taken as "moreover" (= ଆଉର, or Bengali ଆବାର; cf. the Bengali forms in 3.128–3.132); the reading is uncertain.
  172. ଯୋଗାଇଁ — "is fitting" (cf. ଯୋଗ୍ୟ). No ॥ at the line end.
  173. ଅଛୁ is the form in ‑achu (= ଅଛି, "is"; cf. the note on 3.113). "The king of devotees" (bhaktarāja) is apparently Radha Herself, the foremost of devotees; not knowing Her, the queens ask twice. ସୁମରି (= ସ୍ମରି) — "remembering".
  174. The word ≈ ପଦପଙ୍କଜକୁ ("of the lotus feet") is printed with a damaged third letter. ପଡ଼ିବୁ, ନୋହିବୁ — future 1st person plural in ‑ibu.
  175. Chintamani is the wish-fulfilling gem, a name of Krishna (cf. the note on 3.161). Printed ଶୁଣ (without ି); given as ଶୁଣି. "My mouth" is āmbhara (the respectful "Our"). Krishna seems to deny having uttered Radha's name and sends the queens to Vrindavati.
  176. Vrindavati is Vrinda (Vrinda-devi); cf. 2.179 and the note there. The name is printed ≈ ବୃଦାବତୀ (ନ୍ଦ with a sign resembling ଦ, as also ବୃନ୍ଦା in 3.201 and 3.205; the last syllable ତୀ with the sign resembling ଷ with a stroke). ନାମେ is printed with a broken ା. The words ≈ ନ ସ୍ୱାମିଣି are not understood: possibly "[she] who is not (?) a mistress" or "[our] mistress"; the sense is unclear. ≈ ପଚାର ("ask") — the middle letter is printed with a subscript stroke. For Gaudiya Vaishnavas, Vrinda-devi is the goddess of the Vrindavana forest who arranges the meetings of Radha and Krishna (cf. the note on 2.179).
  177. ≈ ସ୍ମରେ ("remembers") is read uncertainly (printed ≈ ସୃ + େ + ର). ମୁହିଁ — "I". ତା' is short for ତାର ("his").
  178. ଯହୁଁ — "when" (archaic). Printed ହେ'ଇଲେ (ା broken off); given as ହୋଇଲେ. "The two queens" are Rukmini and Satyabhama (3.185, 3.187–3.188).
  179. Printed ଫେଡ଼ବୁ (without ି); given as ଫେଡ଼ିବୁ (a future used as a request: "you will dispel" = "dispel"). ≈ ଆପଣ ଭାବରେ is taken as "in their own feeling", "with feeling"; possibly "[said] to you (?)". କରଯୋଡ଼ (printed ≈ କର + େ + ଯା + ଡ଼) = କରଯୋଡ଼ି ("with joined palms").
  180. ଅଟେ — "is" (printed ଅ + hook େ + ଟ); ସେବା — "she, that one". The second half-line is read uncertainly: printed ≈ ନେଲା ନାଥେ କଣି; the last word is taken as କିଣି ("having bought"; there is no ି on କ): "She has bought (won over) the Lord and taken [Him]". No ॥ at the line end.
  181. ସମ୍ଭାଳ (sambhāḷa) — "take care, set right, hold"; taken as a request to Vrinda, and the sense of the second half-line is rendered uncertainly (lit. "taking Her acquaintance (paricaya), take care"). The line ends with "।" instead of ॥.
  182. ଏମଂତେ is printed with a break (ଏମଂ + େ, then ତ). ≈ ସଧୀରେ ("attentively, calmly"; possibly = ସୁଧୀରେ) is read uncertainly. The penultimate word (printed ≈ ବ + ଷି) is taken as ବର୍ଷି ("raining"); possibly ବହି ("flowing").
  183. ଆଜ୍ଞା ("at your command", a respectful reply) is corrected from the edition's errata ("୨୧।୨୫"); in our scan the ligature ଜ୍ଞ is damaged (two dots below). "Her who is the essence of Krishna's body, the light of the world" is apparently Radha (ଯାହା, "which/who", can also refer to the story itself). Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 4: Radha is Krishna's hladini-shakti, mahabhava embodied. No ॥ at the line end.
  184. Printed ≈ ଉଚ୍ଚଟ (the middle letter indistinct, no ା); given as ଉଚ୍ଚାଟ ("agitation, unsettling"). କହିବ, କରିବ — future in ‑iba, used by Kanai also for the 1st person (cf. the note on 3.154).
  185. Printed ନଶ୍ଚେ (without ି); given as ନିଶ୍ଚେ ("surely"). The thought that Krishna comes wherever Radha's name is sounded agrees with the Gaudiya Vaishnava veneration of Radha's name.
  186. ≈ କହ (printed କ + ହ, the same ହ as in ତାହା) — the form is unclear: "tell" (imper.) or, by the sense, "[if I] tell". Vrinda fears that at the story of Radha Krishna Himself will come here (cf. 3.208).
  187. ଉକାଅ is corrected to ଡକାଅ ("call") from the edition's errata ("୨୧।୨୯"). ≈ ବର ("[you] wish, choose"?) is read uncertainly. Kanai calls Subhadra Yogamaya; in the Odia tradition Subhadra is venerated as Yogamaya, the Adya-shakti (cf. 1.55 and the note there); for Gaudiya Vaishnavas Subhadra is Krishna's sister. The story apparently leads to a tradition well known in Puri: the queens of Dvaraka listen to an account of the Vraja pastimes while Subhadra stands at the door, and Krishna and Balarama, coming and hearing it, assume in ecstasy the forms in which They are worshipped in Puri as Jagannatha and Baladeva. This account is not given in the Chaitanya-charitamrita or the Chaitanya-bhagavata; the story continues on p. 22.
  188. Vrinda's speech continues (3.206–3.210). Printed ଆଗୋଳବେ and ଭତରେ (no ି visible); given as ଆଗୋଳିବେ ("will bar") and ଭିତରେ ("inside"). Rama is Balarama. On Subhadra as Yogamaya and the tradition to which the story apparently leads, see the note to 3.210.
  189. "The Master of maya" (māẏādhara) is Krishna. Printed ରେଧିବାକୁ (without ା); given as ରୋଧିବାକୁ ("to hold back"). For Gaudiya Vaishnavas Yogamaya is the Lord's internal energy, which arranges His lilas; that she alone can "hold back" Krishna agrees with this view. The sign resembling ଷ (in kṣama, twice) is କ୍ଷ in this type.
  190. The first word (≈ ସେହିମନ୍ତ, "thus, in that way") is an uncertain reading: the ି and the top of ମ are not visible. The queens are Rukmini and Satyabhama (cf. the note to 3.201). On Vrinda see the note to 3.198.
  191. ≈ ପ୍ରତିହାରିଣୀ ("door-keeper"): the syllable ତି is printed in the sign resembling ଷ with a stroke, the next letter is broken, and no ି is visible after ର; the reading is probable. The next word (≈ ପ୍ରାୟେକ) is not identified: perhaps ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ("apart") or ପ୍ରାନ୍ତେକ ("at the edge [of the door]"). Subhadra keeps watch so that Krishna will not come in and hear the story of Radha (3.208–3.212).
  192. Rohini is Balarama's mother, one of Vasudeva's wives, living in Dvaraka; in the tradition mentioned in the note to 3.210 it is she who tells the queens the lilas of Vraja. In Kanai, Vrinda first expounds the truth about Radha (3.213), then Rohini tells [the story]. ବଖଣୀ corrected to ବଖାଣୀ per the edition's list of errata ("୨୨।୫" — page 22, line 5; the line number matches our count). On ≈ ଗୁଣି see the note to 3.180. The word ≈ ଭବଭକମୟ is not identified; perhaps ଭାବ-ଭକ୍ତିମୟ ("full of bhava and bhakti"). With this couplet the text of the poem in the edition breaks off: the edition gives the poem incomplete, and its continuation is absent from it. Below, the page has only a tailpiece ornament and the printer's imprint; Rohini's account and whatever follows it are missing from the edition.
